entries.appliesTo: controllers and processors doing business in Louisiana that meet a revenue or data-volume threshold ($25M revenue, 75,000+ consumers' data, or 50%+ revenue from selling personal information)

dutySources.impact-assessment: § 1780.4(E)(1) — 'A controller shall conduct and document a data protection assessment of each of the following processing activities involving personal data'
dutySources.consent-workflow: § 1780.4(A)(2)(d) — 'Process the sensitive data of a consumer without obtaining the consumer's consent, or, in the case of processing the sensitive data of a known child, without processing that data in accordance with the rules, regulations, and the exceptions of the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act of 1998'
dutySources.takedown-process: § 1780.3(E)(1) — 'A controller shall establish two or more secure and reliable methods to enable consumers to submit a request to exercise their consumer rights under this Chapter'; § 1780.3(C)(1) — 'A controller shall establish a process for a consumer to appeal the controller's refusal to take action on a request'
dutySources.risk-program: § 1780.4(A)(1)(b) — 'shall establish, implement, and maintain reasonable administrative, technical, and physical data security practices that are appropriate to the volume and nature of the personal data at issue'

exposure.enforcer: attorney-general (violations are unfair trade practices under R.S. 51:1401 et seq., private rights of action excluded)

sources.admOptOut: § 1780.3(A)(2)(e) — 'Opt out of the processing of the personal data for purposes of: (i) Targeted advertising. (ii) The sale of personal data. (iii) Profiling in furtherance of a decision that produces a legal or similarly significant effect concerning the consumer.'
sources.profilingAssessment: § 1780.4(E)(1)(c) — 'The processing of personal data for purposes of profiling, if the profiling presents a reasonably foreseeable risk of any of the following: (i) Unfair or deceptive treatment of or unlawful disparate impact on consumers.'
sources.enforcer: § 1780.5(A) — 'The attorney general shall enforce the provisions of this Chapter.'; § 1780.5(C) — 'Any violation of the provisions of this Chapter shall constitute an unfair and deceptive trade practice pursuant to the Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law, R.S. 51:1401 et seq., excluding private rights of action as provided in R.S. 51:1409 and 1409.1.'
sources.cureDays: § 1780.5(D)(1) — 'Cures the alleged violation identified by the attorney general within the thirty-day period.'
sources.appliesTo: § 1780.2(A) — 'shall apply only to a person or entity that does business in the state and that satisfies one or more of the following thresholds: (1) Has annual gross revenues in excess of twenty-five million dollars. (2) Annually buys, receives for the business's commercial purposes, sells, or shares for commercial purposes the personal information of seventy-five thousand or more consumers, households, or devices. (3) Derives fifty percent or more of its annual revenues from selling consumers' personal information.'

flags: General consumer data privacy act; AI relevance is limited to 'profiling' (defined § 1780.1(24) as 'any form of solely automated processing performed on personal data') — the opt-out right and the data protection assessment trigger.
No penaltyMax coded: enforcement is routed through the Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law, R.S. 51:1401 et seq. (rule 4, no imports).
Cure period is time-limited: the 30-day right-to-cure notice regime applies only 'Beginning January 1, 2027, and ending July 31, 2027' (§ 1780.5(D)).

Privacy-notice duty (§ 1780.4(B)(1) 'reasonably accessible and clear privacy notice') and the mandated sensitive/biometric sale notices ('NOTICE: We may sell your sensitive personal data.') fit no listed duty key.
risk-program is coded for the § 1780.4(A)(1)(b) data-security-practices mandate, not an AI governance program — arguably lossy against the duty definition.
Consumer rights of access, correction, deletion, and portability with a 45-day response deadline and 60-day appeal decision (§ 1780.3(B)(2), (C)(3)) have no param slot in the privacy-data vocabulary.

Child provisions present (sensitive data includes 'Personal data collected from a known child', § 1780.1(29)(c); COPPA parental-consent safe harbor § 1780.2(E)) but the act is not minors-focused, so minorsFocus is not set.
Processor contract requirements (§ 1780.4(D)(2)) and processor assistance duties fit no listed duty key.
Effective January 1, 2027 (Section 2); data protection assessments 'are required for processing activities as of January 1, 2027, and are not retroactive' (§ 1780.4(E)(7)).
